We Fix the Boat We Have

Every spring somebody from the council asks me why Gull Point does not buy a new ferry. Here's the thing: a new ferry is a promise, and an old ferry is a record. I trust records.

We fix the boat we have. That sentence has saved this town more money than any grant. It is not thrift for its own sake. It is knowing your hull.

Plain as rope: the expensive mistakes come from people who want a clean start. There is no clean start on the water. There is the boat, the tide and the crew, in that order.

I write everything down. Fuel, weather, who was late, which bolt sang. Memory is a liar with a nice voice, and a logbook is the only witness that does not get tired.

If you want my whole philosophy, it fits on a cleat. Tell the truth early. Check the knots twice. Fix what you have before you dream about what you don't.
